hits.title: Retrieval Augmented Generation: A Reading Map
hits.text:
## Results
Across the notes we compare, hybrid retrieval improves recall on terminology-heavy questions, and reranking improves the precision of the context passed to the generator. Systems that cite evidence spans produce answers that are easier to audit, but citation coverage must be measured rather than assumed. Retrieval latency is dominated by the first-stage candidate search when the index is warm. The survey also observes that chunk boundaries can change which passage wins a query even when the underlying document is unchanged.

hits.title: Evaluating Retrieval and Grounded Answers
hits.text:
## Method
We build a query set with expected paper identifiers and section titles. Recall at k measures whether any expected section appears in the top k results; MRR records the rank of the first relevant hit. For answers, we count citation coverage as the share of conclusion sentences that carry a valid source marker, and we check each marker against the retrieved chunk list. A citation that points to a non-existent chunk is treated as unknown evidence, not as support. Evaluation runs are stored as JSON so that metrics can be recomputed.

hits.title: Grounding Generated Summaries with Evidence Spans
hits.text:
## Limitations
Citation validity is not entailment. The validator does not verify that the cited sentence actually supports the conclusion, which would require a separate entailment model. Coverage can be gamed by short, trivial sentences. The notes also assume chunk-level evidence rather than character-level spans, so a citation points to a range that may contain more than the cited claim.

hits.title: Grounding Generated Summaries with Evidence Spans
hits.text:
## Results
In our notes, generated summaries have higher readability but occasionally attach a citation to a sentence that overstates the source. The validator catches unknown markers immediately, but it cannot detect a valid marker used for a claim the chunk does not support. Coverage is therefore a necessary but not sufficient check. Extractive fallback has full coverage and lower readability, and it keeps the product usable when the model endpoint is unavailable.

hits.title: Grounding Generated Summaries with Evidence Spans
hits.text:
## Method
Retrieved chunks are numbered C1 through Cn and passed to the generator with a strict instruction to cite them. The validator parses citation markers, checks them against the chunk set, and computes citation coverage as cited conclusion sentences divided by total conclusion sentences. Unknown markers are removed from the visible summary and recorded in a report. If coverage falls below a threshold, or the model call fails, the system returns an extractive summary built from the chunks, with the same citation numbers. Prompt hashes and latency are logged without storing credentials.

hits.title: Reranking for Retrieval Pipelines
hits.text:
## Takeaways
Treat reranking as a precision stage with an explicit budget. Keep the candidate depth configurable and log both first-stage and reranked ranks for debugging. If the generator still sees irrelevant context, inspect the reranker rather than increasing the context window.

hits.title: Retrieval Augmented Generation: A Reading Map
hits.text:
## Takeaways
Start from retrieval quality, then improve the generator. Keep a lexical baseline, add dense retrieval when paraphrase matters, and fuse by rank rather than raw score. Always preserve a path from an answer sentence back to a source passage and its line numbers.

hits.title: Reranking for Retrieval Pipelines
hits.text:
## Limitations
A cross-encoder reranker cannot fix a candidate list that misses the relevant passage entirely. Long passages increase cost and may exceed the reranker's input limit. Training hard negatives from the same retriever can overfit to its failure modes. The notes do not cover learned fusion of multiple rerankers, and nDCG rewards graded relevance that our small corpus does not provide.
